hero.title: Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean Cruises: Best Itineraries and When to Go
hero.subtitle: Intimate luxury yachting meets iconic Caribbean harbors, secluded coves, and bespoke island-hopping voyages.
hero.description: Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean Cruises combine intimate yacht travel with Caribbean destinations ranging from the Bahamas and Turks and Caicos to St. Barths, the British Virgin Islands, St. Lucia, Antigua, the Grenadines and beyond.

paragraphs: The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection's Caribbean program changes by season, with itineraries departing from ports such as Miami, San Juan and Oranjestad. Current and announced collections include short three- and four-night escapes, five- to seven-night island-hopping voyages, and longer Caribbean journeys.
Choosing the right itinerary is about more than picking the longest cruise or the most famous island.

Your ideal Ritz-Carlton Caribbean voyage depends on: Which islands you want to visit; How many nights you have; Whether you prefer beaches or culture; Whether you want a round trip; Whether you want a port-intensive itinerary; Whether you prefer more time aboard the yacht; When you want to travel; Whether you want Miami, San Juan or another departure; Whether you are traveling as a couple, family or group.
This guide explains the major itinerary styles, destinations and seasonal considerations to help you plan a Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean vacation.

quickAnswerTable.title: Quick Answer: What Are the Best Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean Itineraries?
quickAnswerTable.lead: There is no single itinerary that fits every traveler. Instead, different Caribbean routes emphasize different experiences.
rows: Easy logistics and short Caribbean voyages
Chic harbors, beaches and island scenery
Grenadines, St. Lucia, Antigua and island culture
St. Thomas, St. John, Virgin Gorda and neighboring islands
Multiple destinations with an open-jaw itinerary
Easy access to smaller Caribbean islands
quickAnswerTable.takeaway: The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection's current and upcoming programs include more than 20 Caribbean voyages for winter 2026–2027 and an expanded 27-port Caribbean program for winter 2027–2028.

bestTimeOverview.title: When Is the Best Time to Take a Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean Cruise?
bestTimeOverview.subtitle: For travelers seeking the classic Caribbean winter experience, the primary Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean season is concentrated around the cooler months in North America. Current programs show Caribbean voyages extending through the late fall, winter and spring, with the 2026–2027 collection specifically built around winter Caribbean cruising. The best time for you depends on what you prioritize.

features.title: December Through February: Winter Escape
features.description: This period can be attractive for travelers looking for a Caribbean escape during the North American winter. Consider this period if you want: Warm-weather vacation planning, A winter getaway, Holiday or New Year travel, Caribbean beach time, and A break from colder weather.

features.title: March Through April: Spring Cruising
features.description: Spring can be useful for travelers who want a Caribbean vacation before the yacht's seasonal deployment changes. The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection has operated Caribbean itineraries into April in recent seasons, including voyages aboard Evrima and Ilma.

features.title: May Through June: Seasonal Transitions
features.description: The current 2026 program also identifies April through June as a period when voyages operate across Caribbean and Mediterranean destinations, depending on the sailing. If you are considering a spring itinerary, compare the exact sailing rather than assuming every Caribbean itinerary operates year-round.

features.title: Late Fall: Early Season Options
features.description: Some Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean voyages begin during the late fall, making this period relevant for travelers looking for an earlier-season Caribbean escape. The exact route and yacht deployment vary by year.

seasonsAtAGlance.title: Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean Cruise Seasons at a Glance
seasonsAtAGlance.lead: Always check the exact year's itinerary collection before assuming a route is offered during a particular month.
rows: Beginning of Caribbean season on selected itineraries
Selected spring voyages depending on deployment
Caribbean availability may be more limited depending on seasonal deployment
seasonsAtAGlance.takeaway: Seasonal deployment dictates yacht availability between the Caribbean and Mediterranean.

destinationsPartOne.title: Signature Short Escapes & Iconic Luxury Ports
destinationsPartOne.subtitle: Discover the most accessible weekend voyages and prestigious French-Caribbean harbors.

cards.title: 1. Bahamas & Bimini Ritz-Carlton Yacht Cruises
cards.description: The Bahamas are among the easiest Caribbean-region options for travelers looking for a shorter yacht experience. Bimini can work particularly well for travelers who want beaches, clear water, short travel time, a relaxed island atmosphere, and a shorter voyage.
features: Recent Ritz-Carlton programming has included Bimini alongside Miami and Nassau itineraries
The 2027–2028 collection highlights Great Exuma and Key West on shorter round-trip voyages
Best for: New to yacht cruising, limited vacation time, or South Florida residents
Focus on relaxing at sea and unhurried beach time rather than moving between many islands
cards.highlight: The ultimate low-stress trial for travelers new to luxury yacht cruising.

cards.title: 2. Miami Round-Trip Caribbean Cruises
cards.description: Miami is one of the most convenient starting points for Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean voyages. The current winter 2026–2027 program includes departures from Miami, while the announced 2027–2028 season expands short Miami round trips.
features: Simplifies airfare, ground transportation, pre-cruise hotels, and post-cruise planning
Expanded 3- and 4-night round-trip voyages from Miami and San Juan
Ideal for travelers who do not want to take a full week away from work
Seamlessly combine sailing with luxury South Beach or Brickell hotel extensions
cards.highlight: Eliminates open-jaw flight hassles while delivering full yacht luxury.

cards.title: 3. St. Barths Ritz-Carlton Yacht Cruises
cards.description: St. Barths is one of the Caribbean destinations frequently associated with luxury yachting. A Ritz-Carlton itinerary featuring Gustavia, St. Barths appeals to travelers interested in luxury shopping, restaurants, beaches, yacht-filled harbors, and French-Caribbean atmosphere.
features: Current and upcoming itineraries feature St. Barths repeatedly on short and longer routes
Yacht tenders directly into chic Gustavia harbor beside world-class superyachts
Provides access to smaller island destinations while keeping your luxury suite with you
Creates a different experience from staying at one resort and taking day trips
cards.highlight: Experience world-class dining, boutiques, and beaches with your private terrace suite.

bviItineraries.title: British Virgin Islands Itineraries
bviItineraries.subtitle: The British Virgin Islands can be particularly appealing for travelers who prioritize beaches, sailing scenery, snorkeling, small islands, protected coves, and relaxed Caribbean experiences.

cards.title: Virgin Gorda & The Baths
cards.description: Virgin Gorda is world-famous for The Baths, a distinctive coastal landscape of massive granite boulders, hidden tidal grottos, and turquoise water coves.
features: Several current Caribbean itineraries incorporate Virgin Gorda calls
Explore scenic trails winding between ancient sea boulders to Devil's Bay
Calm bays perfect for the yacht's fold-out Marina platform watersports
cards.highlight: One of the most visually stunning natural landscapes in the entire Caribbean.

cards.title: Jost Van Dyke
cards.description: Jost Van Dyke provides a more relaxed island experience, with pristine beaches, famous beachside watering holes, and small-scale Caribbean surroundings.
features: Current three-night San Juan round-trip itineraries include Jost Van Dyke and St. Barths
Anchor in Great Harbour or White Bay for effortless swim-up shore visits
Zero commercial cruise-ship congestion or mass-market crowds
cards.highlight: Authentic, laid-back Caribbean atmosphere surrounded by emerald waters.

cards.title: Norman Island
cards.description: Norman Island is another smaller Caribbean destination appearing in the announced itinerary collection, celebrated as the historic inspiration for Treasure Island.
features: Demonstrates the distinct advantage of smaller yacht deployment over mega-ships
World-class snorkeling at The Caves, The Bight, and The Indians reef formations
Protected waters providing tranquil anchorage and stunning sunset views
cards.highlight: Exclusive yacht access to secluded coves inaccessible to large cruise liners.

scenicDestinations.title: Dramatic Landscapes, Sailing Heritage & Untouched Archipelagos
scenicDestinations.subtitle: Explore volcanic peaks in St. Lucia, maritime history in Antigua, and the idyllic Grenadines.

cards.title: 5. St. Lucia & the Pitons
cards.description: St. Lucia is a strong choice for travelers who want more than beaches. The island combines volcanic scenery, rainforest, coastal views, hiking, cultural experiences, and Caribbean beaches.
features: Current Ritz-Carlton itineraries include Soufrière with panoramic views of the iconic Pitons
Opportunities for guided rainforest exploration, botanical gardens, and sulfur springs
Best for: Nature, hiking, scenic landscapes, photography, and outdoor activities
cards.highlight: Combines rich onshore eco-exploration with oceanfront luxury.

cards.title: 6. Antigua & Falmouth Harbour
cards.description: Antigua provides a different Caribbean experience, combining legendary white-sand beaches, historic Nelson's Dockyard sailing heritage, and protected natural harbors.
features: Current itineraries include Falmouth Harbour on Southern and Eastern Caribbean routes
Rich colonial maritime architecture paired with modern superyacht culture
Works well for travelers interested in sailing, history, harbor scenery, and private tours
cards.highlight: A refined blend of historic harbor atmosphere and private shore excursions.

cards.title: 7. The Grenadines (Bequia & Canouan)
cards.description: The Grenadines can be a compelling option for travelers who want a slower, more scenic Caribbean itinerary. Current itineraries include Bequia, Canouan, St. Lucia, and Grenada.
features: New Year's voyages travel through Bequia, Canouan, Soufrière, Antigua and Virgin Gorda
Smaller islands, pristine coral reefs, scenic sailing, and less urbanized destinations
A slower, restorative pace through exclusive private-island harbors
cards.highlight: Serene, authentic Caribbean beauty far removed from mainstream tourist routes.

departureRoutes.title: Regional Departures & Open-Jaw Routing Styles
departureRoutes.subtitle: Compare San Juan round trips, open-jaw combinations, and comprehensive Southern Caribbean voyages.

cards.title: 8. San Juan Round-Trip Caribbean Cruises
cards.description: San Juan is another important starting point for Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean itineraries, with multiple voyages departing and returning to Puerto Rico.
features: Provides immediate access to BVI, St. Barths, St. Lucia, Martinique, Antigua, and Grenadines
A current six-night San Juan itinerary includes Soufrière, Martinique, Gustavia, and Norman Island
Allows seamless pre- or post-cruise luxury stays in historic Old San Juan or Dorado Beach
cards.highlight: Fastest access to deep Caribbean island-hopping without lengthy open-ocean transit.

cards.title: 9. Miami to San Juan Caribbean Cruises
cards.description: A Miami-to-San Juan itinerary can be useful if you want a more expansive vacation rather than a simple round trip. Listings include a six-night route visiting Grand Turk, Jost Van Dyke, and St. John.
features: Combine: Miami Pre-Cruise → Yacht Voyage → San Juan / Puerto Rico Post-Cruise
Explore multiple distinct Caribbean sub-regions on a single directional voyage
Tradeoff: Requires one-way airfare, additional hotel nights, and coordinated transfers
cards.highlight: The ultimate foundation for a multi-destination luxury land-and-sea vacation.

cards.title: 10. Southern Caribbean Itineraries
cards.description: Southern Caribbean voyages offer a broader geographic range than short Bahamas itineraries, visiting Bequia, Canouan, St. Lucia, Antigua, Grenada, and St. Barths depending on the sailing.
features: Spend more time exploring diverse island cultures rather than taking a short beach trip
Longer port stays and unhurried days at sea aboard Evrima, Ilma, or Luminara
Ideal for seasoned luxury travelers seeking comprehensive Caribbean coverage
cards.highlight: Extensive exploration of authentic Caribbean heritage, cuisine, and scenery.

durationShowcase.title: Which Ritz-Carlton Caribbean Itinerary Is Right for You?
durationShowcase.subtitle: Instead of choosing by destination popularity alone, start with your available vacation timeframe.

pillars.title: If You Have 3–4 Nights: Short Escapes
pillars.description: Look at Miami round trips, San Juan round trips, Bahamas, Bimini, Key West, and St. Barths combinations. The 2027–2028 program specifically expands three- and four-night round-trip voyages from Miami and San Juan for long-weekend escapes.

pillars.title: If You Have 5–7 Nights: Island-Hopping
pillars.description: Look for British Virgin Islands, St. Lucia, Antigua, St. Barths, and Southern Caribbean multi-island routes. Current collections include five- to seven-night voyages across multiple Caribbean regions balancing exploration with yacht relaxation.

pillars.title: If You Have More Than a Week: Grand Voyages
pillars.description: Consider longer itineraries that combine more Caribbean destinations or connect different regions. The longer you sail, the more important it becomes to compare the pace of the itinerary rather than simply counting the number of ports.

pillars.title: Open-Jaw Itineraries: Land + Sea Extensions
pillars.description: Consider Miami to San Juan open-jaw routes allowing you to add luxury pre-cruise Miami hotel stays, private transfers, and post-cruise Puerto Rico resort extensions for a complete luxury holiday.

travelerPersonas.title: Best Ritz-Carlton Caribbean Itineraries by Traveler Style
travelerPersonas.subtitle: Match your personal vacation priorities to the ideal Caribbean sailing format.

cards.title: Best for Couples
cards.description: Couples should prioritize itineraries featuring St. Barths, Virgin Gorda, St. Lucia, Jost Van Dyke, Bequia, and Canouan, combining beaches, scenic surroundings, fine dining, and boutique shopping.
features: Short 3- to 4-night sailings minimize time away from professional schedules
6- to 8-night itineraries provide deeper relaxation for anniversaries and milestones
Enjoy open-seating fine dining, private terrace breakfasts, and tranquil pool decks
cards.highlight: Sophisticated romantic escapes with zero mega-ship noise or formal night pressure.

cards.title: Best for Honeymoons
cards.description: For a honeymoon, consider the entire trip rather than just the yacht. Combine city luxury with private yacht sailing and secluded Caribbean beach extensions.
features: Days 1–2: 5-star Miami or San Juan luxury hotel stay
Days 3–8: Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean island-hopping voyage
Final Days: Caribbean land resort or private villa extension
An advisor coordinates private transfers, suites, and VIP Virtuoso amenities
cards.highlight: The perfect balance of vibrant city culture, private terrace cruising, and beach seclusion.

cards.title: Best for First-Time Yacht Travelers
cards.description: First-time yacht travelers may prefer a shorter itinerary. A three- or four-night voyage provides an introduction to suite accommodations, yacht service, dining, and life at sea without requiring a two-week commitment.
features: The 2027–2028 collection specifically features short Miami & San Juan voyages
Experience Suite Ambassador care, marina platform sports, and premium dining
Low risk of travel fatigue with convenient Florida hub departures
cards.highlight: Discover the intimate yachting lifestyle before booking longer worldwide voyages.

cards.title: Best for Beach Lovers
cards.description: If beaches are your priority, look closely at itineraries featuring Bimini, Great Exuma, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, Canouan, Bequia, and St. Barths.
features: Direct ocean access from the yacht's fold-out Marina platform
Pristine white-sand coves with complimentary watersports gear
Remember that beach appeal depends on specific shore experiences and weather conditions
cards.highlight: Swim, kayak, and lounge at world-renowned Caribbean beaches.

cards.title: Best for Nature & Active Lovers
cards.description: If you want more than beaches, consider routes featuring St. Lucia, Dominica, Virgin Gorda, St. John, Grenada, and Southern Caribbean destinations.
features: Lush rainforest landscapes, volcanic peaks, and protected national parkland
Coral-rich waters for world-class guided snorkeling and scuba diving
Active onshore hiking, waterfalls, and botanical discovery tours
cards.highlight: Explore dynamic Caribbean ecosystems alongside 5-star yacht comfort.

cards.title: Best for Food & Culture
cards.description: For travelers prioritizing culture and cuisine, consider itineraries including San Juan, St. Barths, Martinique, Antigua, Puerto Plata, Samaná, and Cartagena on longer voyages.
features: Locally inspired Caribbean cuisine and fresh seafood featured in onboard menus
Explore historic UNESCO colonial fortresses, rum distilleries, and French gastronomy
Bespoke private food tours and market visits curated by yacht concierges
cards.highlight: Immerse yourself in authentic island flavors and centuries of Caribbean heritage.

angelaPerspective.bio: Angela Hughes is CEO of Trips & Ships Luxury Travel and founder of Luxury Travel University. Her career spans more than four decades in the travel industry, with experience across luxury cruises, international travel and customized premium travel.
angelaPerspective.text: Caribbean yachting is about finding the right cadence. A 3-night Miami escape to Bimini aboard Ilma is vastly different from a 7-night Southern Caribbean voyage through Bequia and the Grenadines. My role is to help you look at the complete journey—evaluating sea days, suite layouts, pre-cruise Miami or San Juan luxury hotels, and custom shore excursions—so you enjoy a frictionless, unforgettable Caribbean vacation.

faqs.question: What is the best month for a Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruise?
faqs.answer: There is no single best month for every traveler. The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection operates Caribbean voyages across different periods depending on the year, with winter and spring featuring prominently in current collections.

faqs.question: Where do Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruises go?
faqs.answer: Depending on the itinerary, destinations include Bimini, Great Exuma, St. Barths, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, St. Lucia, Antigua, Bequia, Canouan and other Caribbean ports.

faqs.question: Does Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection sail from Miami?
faqs.answer: Yes. Miami is a current and upcoming Caribbean turnaround port, with short and longer voyages offered depending on the season.

faqs.question: Does Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection sail from San Juan?
faqs.answer: Yes. San Juan is another major Caribbean departure and turnaround point, with round-trip and other Caribbean itineraries.

faqs.question: Are there short Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruises?
faqs.answer: Yes. The announced 2027–2028 collection includes three- and four-night round-trip voyages from Miami and San Juan.

faqs.question: What are the best Ritz-Carlton Caribbean destinations for couples?
faqs.answer: Couples may want to compare itineraries featuring St. Barths, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, St. Lucia, Bequia and Canouan based on their interests.

faqs.question: Which Ritz-Carlton Caribbean itinerary is best for beaches?
faqs.answer: Itineraries featuring destinations such as Bimini, Great Exuma, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, Canouan and Bequia can be relevant for travelers prioritizing beaches.

faqs.question: Which Ritz-Carlton Caribbean itinerary is best for nature?
faqs.answer: Routes featuring St. Lucia, Dominica, St. John and other nature-focused destinations can provide opportunities for hiking, rainforest, volcanic scenery and marine activities.

faqs.question: Is St. Barths included on Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean itineraries?
faqs.answer: Yes. Current and announced itineraries include multiple St. Barths calls, including Gustavia.

faqs.question: Does Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection visit the British Virgin Islands?
faqs.answer: Yes. Current itineraries include destinations such as Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and Norman Island.

faqs.question: Does Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection visit St. Lucia?
faqs.answer: Yes. Current Caribbean itineraries include Soufrière and other St. Lucia experiences.

faqs.question: What is the best Ritz-Carlton Caribbean itinerary for first-time yacht travelers?
faqs.answer: A short three- or four-night itinerary can provide an introduction to yacht travel without requiring a longer vacation. Current future collections include these shorter voyages from Miami and San Juan.

faqs.question: Is winter a good time for a Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruise?
faqs.answer: Winter is a major period for the Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection's Caribbean program, including the current 2026–2027 collection.

faqs.question: Can I take a Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruise during the holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes. The collection has offered holiday and New Year's Caribbean sailings, including Southern Caribbean voyages.

faqs.question: What happens if weather affects a Caribbean itinerary?
faqs.answer: Weather can affect ports, excursions or sailing schedules. Travelers should review the cruise line's current terms and consider appropriate travel insurance when planning Caribbean travel.

faqs.question: Are Ritz-Carlton Caribbean shore excursions included?
faqs.answer: Shore excursions are generally separate from the standard onboard inclusions and should be evaluated based on the specific voyage and experience.

faqs.question: How many nights should I spend on a Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruise?
faqs.answer: Three to four nights can work for short escapes, five to seven nights can provide more island exploration, and longer voyages can support a slower, more extensive Caribbean itinerary.

faqs.question: Is Miami or San Juan better for a Ritz-Carlton Caribbean cruise?
faqs.answer: The answer depends on the itinerary, travel logistics and destinations you want to visit. Miami is particularly useful for Florida and U.S. travelers, while San Juan provides convenient access to many Eastern and Southern Caribbean routes.

finalAnswer.title: Final Takeaway: Choosing Your Ritz-Carlton Caribbean Voyage
finalAnswer.lead: Ritz-Carlton Yacht Caribbean Cruises offer several different ways to experience the region, from short Miami escapes to longer Southern and Eastern Caribbean voyages.
paragraphs: The current and announced collections include itineraries featuring destinations such as Bimini, Great Exuma, St. Barths, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, St. Lucia, Antigua, Bequia and Canouan, with departure options including Miami and San Juan.

When choosing your itinerary, consider: Where you want to go, How many nights you have, What season you prefer, Whether you want a round trip, How much time you want at sea, Which shore experiences interest you, Which yacht and suite you prefer, and Whether you want to add Miami, San Juan or another land stay.

For a short first yacht experience, look at the three- and four-night options. For island exploration, compare five- to seven-night routes. For a honeymoon, anniversary or extended luxury vacation, consider a longer itinerary combined with pre- or post-cruise hotel stays.
The most important step is to compare the entire itinerary—not simply the number of ports—against the kind of Caribbean vacation you want to have.
